newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti to stay in red for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti to stay in red for 1997.

text.p: Italy's Olivetti is set to stay in the red for 1997, the group reported on Wednesday, as improvements in its information technology companies fail to offset losses from its telecoms operations.

Group chief executive Roberto Colaninno told Olivetti's annual shareholders meeting in its home town of Ivrea, near Turin in northwest Italy, that 1997 would see a recovery in profitability in its information technology interests.

This would see positive results in 1997 for Olsy (Olivetti Solutions) producing computer systems for banking and retailers, Lexikon which makes printers, copiers and fax machines and its 48 percent-owned specialist information systems group Tecnost.

But Olivetti's telecoms interests, Telemedia and its 35.5 percent stake in mobile phone consortium Omnitel, would stay in loss for 1997. However, these losses were in line with the company's internal budget.

"The positive effects from the results in information technology will not be sufficient to completely cover the losses of the telecoms companies and the costs of the holding company," Colaninno told shareholders.
"We anticipate a consolidated result that therefore represents an important progress towards a return to conditions of economic equilibrium," he added.
But Colaninno stuck with his forecast that the group will get as close as possible to break-even in 1997 before Omnitel's losses and before tax payments.

He repeated his forecast given at an analysts' meeting last month that Olivetti's sales would reach nine trillion lire in 1997 after 8.3 trillion in 1996, with seven trillion coming from its information technology companies and around 25 percent, or two trillion lire, from telecoms.

At that meeting in May, Colaninno said that he expected Olivetti in the first half of 1997 to make a pretax loss, excluding Omnitel's losses, of 264.2 billion against a loss of 350.2 billion in the first half of 1996.
The group, which has not recorded a profit since 1990, had net losses in 1996 of 915 billion lire, down from a 1.6 trillion lire loss in 1995.
